name: Barbados
description: Barbados offers expats an idyllic Caribbean lifestyle characterized by stunning beaches, a warm climate, and a welcoming community. The island provides a stable political and economic environment, with modern infrastructure and attractive tax benefits for residents and remote workers.
longdescription: Barbados presents an appealing destination for expats seeking a high quality of life within a vibrant Caribbean setting. The culture is a rich blend of African, Indian, and British influences, fostering a friendly and hospitable society where respect and good manners are highly valued. English is the official language, though the lively Bajan dialect is commonly spoken, reflecting the island's unique heritage. The economy is primarily service-driven, with tourism and international business playing significant roles, complemented by a growing remote-work community. The Barbadian dollar is pegged to the US dollar, providing currency predictability. Expat communities are visible and welcoming, especially among digital nomads and retirees, though deeper integration with locals builds gradually through consistent interaction and respect for local norms. The pace of life is generally slower, embracing a concept often referred to as 'island time,' which new residents should be prepared to adapt to. The government is stable, operating under a parliamentary system with a long tradition of democracy. Healthcare facilities are a mix of public and private, with private options often recommended for expats. Education is a priority, with several reputable private and international schools available for families.

visas.name: Barbados Welcome Stamp
visas.description: The Barbados Welcome Stamp is a special work visa introduced in July 2020 for digital nomads and persons who work in a location-independent manner. It grants eligible applicants the right to live and remotely work in Barbados for one year.
benefits: Exempt from Barbados income tax.
Ability to open and hold an External Bank Account or Foreign Currency Account in Barbados.
Can apply for a Barbados ID.
School-aged children approved under the program do not require a separate Student Visa application.
No requirement to furnish a return ticket on arrival in Barbados.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The Welcome Stamp itself does not provide a direct pathway to citizenship. Holders seeking citizenship must transition to another immigration category, such as the Special Entry and Residence Permit (SERP). After at least seven years of ordinary residence, including at least five years of physical presence, one may apply for Barbadian citizenship.
required_documents: Valid passport
Two passport-sized photographs
Copy of the bio-data page of the passport (for the individual and any accompanying family members)
Copy of birth certificate (for the individual and any accompanying family members)
Proof of relationship of dependants (e.g., birth certificate, marriage or adoption documents)
Entry visa (where applicable)
Proof of suitable accommodation in Barbados (though not always explicitly requested upon application, it's a requirement for stay)
visas.target_applicant: Remote workers, freelancers, entrepreneurs, and families earning income from outside Barbados who wish to live and work remotely from the island.
visas.renewal_conditions: The visa can be renewed for another year, subject to approval and payment of the requisite fee. A 25% discount on the visa fee applies for renewals. Applicants must continue to meet the eligibility requirements.
application_process_steps: Complete the online application form on the official Barbados Welcome Stamp website.
Upload required documents, including passport-sized photographs, passport bio-data page, birth certificates, and proof of relationship for dependents.
Submit your application online.
Wait for a decision via email from the Chief Immigration Officer, typically within 7 working days.
Upon approval, pay the application fee.
Receive your Barbados Welcome Stamp.
visas.tax_implications: Welcome Stamp holders are exempt from Barbados income tax, as income must be generated from outside Barbados and is not considered Barbados-source income. They are, however, subject to Barbados' 17.5% VAT on any products and services purchased on the island.

visas.name: Barbados Retirement Visa
visas.description: The Barbados Special Entry and Reside Permit (SERP) for Retired Property Owners allows eligible non-nationals who own property in Barbados to reside on the island for extended or indefinite periods. It is specifically designed for retirees demonstrating financial self-sufficiency and property ownership, providing a pathway to long-term residency in Barbados.
benefits: Long-term or indefinite residency in Barbados (indefinite for those over 60)
Ability to enter and depart Barbados freely
Path to permanent residency and eventually citizenship
No limitations on length of stay for eligible permit holders
Enjoy Barbados' high quality of life in a stable environment
visas.path_to_residency_description: The SERP grants long-term residency, which can be indefinite for retired property owners aged 60 and over. After five years of continuous legal residency in Barbados, individuals become eligible to apply for Barbadian citizenship.
required_documents: Completed Extension of Stay form (Form B)
Applicant's Birth Certificate (original and photocopy)
Police Certificate of Character from any country resided in for 6 months or more after age 16
Title Deeds or Land Tax document as proof of property ownership in Barbados (property valued at US$300,000 or more)
Proof of financial resources to support self and dependents (e.g., bank statements, pension documents)
Health insurance valid in Barbados
Passport-size photo
Certified copy of the bio-data page of the passport
Marriage certificate (if applicable)
Proof of relationship to dependents (if applicable)

visas.name: Special Entry and Reside Permit (SERP) - Category 1 (Permanent Residence indefinite)
visas.description: The Special Entry and Reside Permit (SERP) - Category 1 is Barbados' residence-by-investment program for high-net-worth individuals. It grants indefinite residency in Barbados, with the specific duration varying based on the applicant's age at the time of application. Holders can also automatically obtain a work permit in Barbados.
visas.target_applicant: High-net-worth individuals who can make a significant investment in Barbados from external funds and demonstrate a substantial net worth.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The SERP Category 1 itself grants residency. After five years of lawful residence as a SERP holder, applicants may apply for immigrant status. After a further five years as an immigrant, permanent resident status may be sought. Commonwealth citizens and Irish nationals may apply for citizenship by naturalization after seven years of ordinary residence (with at least five as an immigrant); other nationals may apply under the Barbados Citizenship Act, Cap. 186.
visas.renewal_conditions: For applicants under 60 years old, the permit is initially granted for renewable 5-year terms (or 5-10 years for those 50-60). Renewal requires a US $5,000 fee per adult and resubmission of documentation to demonstrate continued compliance. Upon reaching age 60, the permit converts to an indefinite (non-expiring) term without further renewal required. Dependents enrolled at a Barbados university must submit schooling evidence every 3 years.
visas.tax_implications: SERP holders can claim a Foreign Currency Tax Credit (FCTC) for foreign-sourced income that is transferred to Barbados through the banking system. This can reduce the effective tax rate to as low as 2.45%. Barbados does not levy capital gains tax, inheritance tax, or wealth tax. Income tax rates are 12.5% on the first BBD 50,000 of taxable income and 28.5% above that threshold. SERP holders spending more than 182 days per year in Barbados are required to declare tax residency with the Barbados Revenue Authority. There are no mandatory minimum physical presence requirements, allowing holders to manage global investments without being forced into Barbadian tax residency.
benefits: Obtain residency in Barbados for the applicant, spouse, and dependent children.
Indefinite residency for applicants aged 60 and over, or a path to indefinite residency for those under 60.
Automatic entitlement to apply for a work permit in Barbados.
Potential path to Barbadian citizenship after meeting residency requirements.
Access to a Foreign Currency Tax Credit (FCTC) for foreign-sourced income transferred to Barbados, potentially reducing the effective tax rate.
No capital gains tax, inheritance tax, or wealth tax in Barbados.
Minimal physical presence requirements, suitable for individuals maintaining an international lifestyle.
required_documents: Completed Form B: Application for Permission to Vary Period of Stay in Barbados or Conditions of Stay.
Application fee of US $150.00.
Proof of health insurance with coverage exceeding US $500,000.00.
Police Certificate of Character (PCC) from any country where the applicant resided for six months or more after age 16 (British applicants require an enhanced disclosure certificate).
One passport-sized photograph.
Original and copy of birth certificate.
Certified copy of the bio-data page of the applicant's valid passport.
Marriage certificate (if applicable).
Proof of relationship to dependents (e.g., birth certificates, legal documents) where applicable.
Certified statement of assets exceeding US $5 million from an auditor or broker.
Evidence of investment in Barbados with a value of at least US $2 million from foreign-sourced funds.
Certified English translations of all non-English documents by an approved translator.
application_process_steps: Obtain Form B: Application for Permission to Vary Period of Stay in Barbados or Conditions of Stay, from the Barbados Immigration Department website or in person.
Complete the application form and gather all required supporting documents.
Submit the completed form along with all supporting documents and the non-refundable US $150.00 application fee.
An initial eligibility assessment is conducted, typically within approximately 5 working days.
The full application is reviewed by the Chief Immigration Officer.
Upon approval, pay the applicable SERP fee (US $5,000 for applicants aged 60 or older, US $3,500 for those under 60; specific fees apply for renewals and different age brackets).
If intending to work, a separate work permit application must be duly submitted to the Immigration Department, subject to additional fees.

visas.name: Special Entry and Reside Permit (SERP) - Category 2 (Renewable 5-year residence)
visas.description: The Special Entry and Reside Permit (SERP) - Category 2 is a long-term residence permit designed for foreign nationals who own real estate in Barbados. It allows qualified individuals, their spouses, and children to obtain residency status in Barbados.
visas.target_applicant: Retired foreign nationals, and applicants under 60, who own real estate in Barbados valued at a minimum of USD $300,000, purchased with foreign-sourced funds, and can demonstrate financial self-sufficiency for the duration of the permit.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After five years of lawful residence as a SERP holder, applicants may apply for immigrant status; after a further five years as an immigrant, permanent resident status may be sought. Commonwealth citizens and Irish nationals may apply for citizenship by naturalisation after seven years of ordinary residence (with at least five as an immigrant); other nationals may apply under the Barbados Citizenship Act.
visas.renewal_conditions: The Category 2 SERP is renewable every 5 years for a fee. For applicants under 60, it converts to an indefinite permit upon reaching age 60.
visas.tax_implications: SERP holders are required to declare tax residency in writing to the Barbados Revenue Authority. They may claim a Foreign Currency Tax Credit (FCTC) for foreign-sourced income transferred to Barbados via the banking system, which can reduce the effective tax rate. Barbados has no capital gains or inheritance taxes.
benefits: Long-term renewable residency in Barbados.
Includes spouse and dependents.
Path to permanent residency and eventual citizenship after five years of lawful residence.

Residents may enjoy fiscal benefits, including freedom from capital gains and inheritance tax, and a foreign currency tax credit on assessable income sourced outside Barbados and transferred to the Barbadian banking system.
No physical presence requirement to maintain residency status (unlike some other schemes).
required_documents: Completed Form B – Application for Permission to Vary Period of Stay in Barbados or Conditions of Stay.
Cover letter.
Evidence of health insurance with minimum per annum coverage of US$500,000, valid in Barbados for the duration of the SERP period.
Police Certificate of Character (PCC) from any country where the applicant has resided for six months or more after the age of 16 (Enhanced disclosure certificate for British applicants).
One passport-sized photo.
Original birth certificate and a copy.
Certified copy of the bio-data page of the applicant's passport.
Marriage certificate, if applicable.
Proof of relationship to dependents where applicable (birth certificates/legal documents).
Proof of property ownership in Barbados, with the property valued at a minimum of US$300,000 (purchased with foreign-sourced funds).
Evidence of financial means to support themselves and dependents for the duration of the permit (e.g., bank statements, pension documents, investment income proof).
Official translations for any documents not originally in English.
application_process_steps: Choose the government-approved investment route (real estate ownership of at least US$300,000 for Category 2).
Complete Form B – Application for Permission to Vary Period of Stay in Barbados or Conditions of Stay.
Gather all necessary documents, including proof of funds, health certificates, and police records.
Pay the non-refundable application fee.
Submit the application and supporting documents to the Barbados Immigration Department.
Undergo a background check and receive the Special Entry and Residence Permit (SERP) upon approval.

visas.name: Long-Term Work Permit
visas.description: The Barbados Long-Term Work Permit is designed for non-nationals seeking extended employment in Barbados. It allows individuals to live and work on the island for a period of up to three years, with the possibility of renewal, under the sponsorship of a Barbadian employer.
visas.target_applicant: This permit is ideal for professionals, specialized technical experts, teachers, and IT professionals whose skills are deemed necessary and cannot be fulfilled by a Barbadian national or resident.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After living in Barbados for five consecutive years on a valid visa (such as the Long-Term Work Permit), individuals may be eligible to apply for permanent residency. This does not automatically grant permanent residency but opens the path for application.
visas.renewal_conditions: Employer can apply for an extension after the initial period; generally requires continued proof that no local or Barbadian national is suitable for the job.
visas.tax_implications: Foreign workers contribute to and are entitled to social security benefits on the same basis as Barbadian nationals. Standard Barbadian resident tax rules apply unless specific exemptions are granted by other schemes (which are not part of this work permit).
benefits: Legal authorization to live and work in Barbados for up to 3 years
Opportunity for renewal after the initial validity period
Potential path to permanent residency after five consecutive years of lawful residence
Contribution to social security benefits on the same basis as Barbadian nationals
May allow family members to join the principal applicant via a dependent visa
required_documents: C-1 and C-2 work permit forms (in duplicate)
Completed Medical Form, including external X-rays in report form
4 passport-sized photos
2 character references on the applicant
Evidence of applicant's qualifications
A detailed cover letter from the potential employer outlining the nature of the business, period of employment, category of employment, and reason for the request
Police Certificate of Character (PCC) from each country lived in for at least 6 months in the past 3 years (or sworn affidavit for UK, plus nationwide search certificate)
Copy of the bio-data page of applicant's valid passport
Proof of employer's justification that no Barbadian national is suitable for the job (e.g., local job advertisement)
application_process_steps: Receive a job offer from a Barbadian employer.
The employer (sponsor) must advertise the vacancy locally to demonstrate no suitable Barbadian national or resident is available for the position.
Gather all required documents, including completed C-1 and C-2 forms, medical report, passport photos, character references, qualifications, and police certificate of character.
The employer submits the completed application and supporting documents to the Barbados Immigration Department.
Pay the application fee upon submission.
Await a decision from the Immigration Department (processing can take approximately 3 weeks to 60 days).

visas.name: Student Visa
visas.description: The Barbados Student Visa is for non-immigrant students who wish to pursue a course of study at a recognized educational institution in Barbados. It allows foreign nationals to lawfully enter and reside in Barbados for educational purposes.
visas.target_applicant: Foreign nationals who have been accepted by a Barbados educational institution, including university, language, secondary school students, vocational trainees, and exchange students.
visas.renewal_conditions: Submission of H-3 Application form, copy of biodata page of passport, one passport sized photograph, previous Student Visa Permit, copy of Student's Current Report, proof of parents' or guardians' status in Barbados (for those under 18 years), and application fee of Bds $300.00.
benefits: Enter Barbados legally for study
Remain in Barbados during the approved course of study
Ability to extend status if studies continue and rules allow
Study full time at the approved institution
Potentially bring dependents in some cases, subject to approval
required_documents: Certificate of Eligibility for Non-immigrant Student Status (Form H-1), completed by school official and certified by the Ministry of Education
Certificate by Non-Immigrant Student (Form H-2), completed by prospective student
Applicant's original birth certificate or notarized copy
Two (2) passport-sized photographs
Copy of biodata page of the applicant's passport
Evidence of financial support adequate for payment of school expenses, living, and medical expenses (e.g., scholarships, bank balances, legal document of support)
A Certificate of Character from the Police of each country where the applicant has lived for at least 6 months in the past 3 years
Letter of acceptance from a school registered/chartered by the Ministry of Education
Timetable and Course Outline
Proof of Accommodation
Applicant's marriage certificate (where applicable)
Letter of consent from parent signed by a notary public (for minors under 18)
Private medical insurance documentation
Proof of travel (e.g., return ticket or evidence of funds for one)
application_process_steps: Obtain acceptance into a recognized educational institution in Barbados.
Complete Certificate of Eligibility for Non-immigrant Student Status (Form H-1) and Certificate by Non-Immigrant Student (Form H-2).
Have Form H-1 completed by the school official and certified by the Ministry of Education.
Gather all required supporting documents, including proof of financial support, police certificate, proof of accommodation, and medical insurance.
Submit the completed forms and all supporting documents to the Barbados Immigration Department (or through the institution's international office).
Pay the non-refundable application fee.
The Immigration Department will assess financial evidence and conduct security clearance.
A provisional student visa may be issued, contingent on favorable security clearance and financial support.

visas.name: Permanent Residency
visas.description: Permanent Resident Status in Barbados allows individuals to reside indefinitely in the country. It is a pathway for foreign nationals who have established a long-term connection to Barbados and demonstrate they will not become a financial burden on the nation. This status is a prerequisite for eventually applying for Barbadian citizenship.
visas.target_applicant: Individuals who have lived in Barbados for a significant period (e.g., five consecutive years) on a valid visa and have integrated into the Barbadian society and economy.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Permanent Residency is the status itself. After five years of continuous residence as a permanent resident, individuals become eligible to apply for Barbadian citizenship.
visas.renewal_conditions: Permanent Residency status itself is indefinite, but conditions for maintaining it are generally tied to not becoming a charge on the nation and adhering to laws.
benefits: Indefinite right to live in Barbados.
Path to Barbadian citizenship after fulfilling further residency requirements.
Ability to work in Barbados (implied by 'Letter of employment' document and general status as a resident).
Family reunification (implied by marriage and birth certificates for dependents).
required_documents: Applicant's Birth Certificate.
Marriage Certificate (if applicable, especially for married women or those married to a Barbadian national).
Death Certificate or Divorce document (Decree Absolute) if previous marriage was terminated.
Mother's Birth Certificate and Parents' Marriage Certificate (if born in wed-lock to a Barbadian mother and a non-national father).
General Medical Certificate of Health from Doctor (if 16 years of age or under).
Completed standard Medical Form by a Doctor (if 16 years of age or over).
Certificate of Character from the Police of each country lived in for at least 6 months in the past 3 years.
Four (4) passport-sized photographs, one certified by a Justice of the Peace or Notary Public.
Letters from school(s) attended in Barbados.
Letter of employment.
Proof of qualifications (if any).
Affidavit to clarify any discrepancies in names on documents.
Notarised Letter of Consent from parent(s) if applicant is under 18 and forms are signed by a person other than the parent(s).
Document showing legal custody if applicable for a child.
Passport Biometrics page (implied from citizenship requirements, likely for PR as well).
application_process_steps: Gather all required documents as listed by the Immigration Department.
Complete the application form (Form A1 for Registration as a Permanent Resident).
Pay the application fee of Bds. $300.00 upon submission (personal cheques are not accepted).
Submit the application to the Immigration Department.
If approved, pay a final fee of Bds. $1200.00.

visas.name: Special Entry Permit (Retirement) / Barbados Retirement Program
visas.description: The Special Entry Permit (SEP), also known as the Special Entry and Reside Permit (SERP), allows non-nationals, particularly retirees and high-net-worth individuals, to reside in Barbados for extended, often indefinite, periods. It grants freedom to visit the island often and stay for as long as desired.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are retired foreign property owners over the age of 50 or 60, or high-net-worth individuals, who can financially support themselves and their dependents.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Retirees over 60 with sufficient means of support can apply for Immigrant Status, which after five years, entitles them to apply for permanent residence. SEP holders can also apply for permanent residency after 5 years.
visas.renewal_conditions: For those under 60, the permit is valid until they reach 60, at which point it must be renewed as an indefinite permit. Ongoing property ownership and maintaining financial status are generally required.
visas.tax_implications: After 182-183 days, an individual becomes a tax resident, meaning they are taxed on worldwide income at rates ranging from 20% to 35%. Pension income exceeding the personal allowance ($40,000 BBD for pensioners over 60) is taxed. Retirement savings from abroad are generally not taxed, and double taxation treaties exist with several countries.
benefits: Long-term or indefinite residency in Barbados, especially for those over 60.
Freedom to enter and depart Barbados without limits on the length of stay.
Path to permanent residency after five years of residence.
Ability to include spouse and dependent children.
Potential to purchase a work permit for some categories (though generally not for the property-owner retirement category).
required_documents: Extension of Stay form.
Applicant's Birth Certificate.
Police Certificate of Character (PCC) from any country resided in for 6 months or more after age 16 (or Enhanced disclosure form for British applicants).
Title Deeds (if applicable).
Land Tax document (if applicable).
Proof of financial resources (e.g., bank statements, pension document).
Health insurance (coverage valid in Barbados, some sources suggest over US$500,000 for those over 50, or US$350,000 for under 50s).
Proof of high net worth (if applicable).
application_process_steps: Gather required documents, including birth certificate, police certificate of character, and proof of financial resources.
Obtain health insurance valid in Barbados.
Complete and submit the Special Entry Permit application form (e.g., Extension of Stay form) to the Barbados Immigration Department.
Pay the applicable permit fees based on age and category.
Await processing and approval from the Barbados Immigration Department.

visas.name: Family / Dependent Visa
visas.description: The Barbados Family / Dependent Visa refers to immigration permission granted to qualifying family members to enter and/or reside in Barbados based on their relationship to a Barbadian citizen or a foreign national who already holds lawful immigration status in Barbados. This permission aims to support family unity and allows for longer lawful stays than a typical tourist visa.
visas.target_applicant: This route is most suitable for spouses of Barbadian citizens or lawful foreign residents, minor children, and potentially other close dependents who are financially supported by the principal applicant.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Long-term lawful residence under this status, especially marriage to a Barbadian citizen or permanent resident, can lead to permanent residency and eventually citizenship. Standard naturalization in Barbados typically requires five years of continuous legal residence.
visas.renewal_conditions: Often possible if the sponsor's status continues and the dependent remains eligible.
benefits: Supports family unity and reunification.
Can allow for a longer lawful stay than standard tourist visas.
May create a platform for future residence regularization in Barbados.
Allows accompanying a principal work permit holder, resident, investor, or student.
Dependent children may attend school in Barbados.
required_documents: Valid passport.
Invitation letter from the host (for family reunion visa).
Marriage certificate (for spouses).
Birth certificate (for children).
Proof of relationship to the principal applicant (for Welcome Stamp family applications).
Cover letter (for family reunion visa).
Proof of sufficient financial means.
Proof of accommodation in Barbados.
application_process_steps: Determine the exact family category available for your situation.
Visit the official Barbados Immigration Department website or a diplomatic mission.
Fill out and submit the visa application form.
Pay the applicable visa application fee at the consular office.
Await processing of the application.

extra_info:
### Visas & Notes
- Barbados Welcome Stamp: 12-month remote work visa available online
- Retirement visa available for those with passive income
- Citizens of CARICOM countries have freedom of movement

Citizenship by Descent.desc: Citizenship by descent is available for children born abroad to at least one Barbadian parent. If born in wedlock, the father must be a citizen; if out of wedlock, the mother must be a citizen. The child must be registered with the nearest Barbadian diplomatic representative.

Naturalization.desc: Foreign nationals can apply for citizenship by naturalization after a period of legal residence. This typically requires having lived in Barbados for the twelve months immediately preceding the application, and for at least five years in aggregate during the seven years before that period, amounting to approximately seven to eight years of residence. Applicants must demonstrate good character and an intention to continue living in Barbados. Commonwealth citizens and citizens of Ireland apply by registration, while others apply by naturalization, with broadly similar residence requirements.

Birthright.desc: If you were born in Barbados after independence on November 29, 1966, you are generally a citizen by birth (jus soli), with the main exception being children born to foreign diplomats posted to Barbados.

Spouse and Family.desc: A foreign woman who has married a citizen of Barbados may apply for citizenship through registration. Spouses of Barbadian citizens can qualify after a defined period of genuine, subsisting marriage and residence.

tax_advice:
*   **Resident Taxation:** Residents are taxed on their worldwide income. The top income tax rate for income year 2026 is 28.50%.
*   **Non-Resident Taxation:** Non-residents are taxed only on their Barbados-sourced income.
*   **Digital Nomads (Welcome Stamp Holders):** Individuals on the Barbados Welcome Stamp visa are deemed non-resident for income tax purposes and continue to pay tax in their home jurisdiction on foreign-earned income.
*   **Corporate Tax:** The general corporate tax rate is 9%, with a reduced rate of 5.5% for companies with a Foreign Currency Permit.
*   **VAT (Value Added Tax):** The standard VAT rate is 17.5%. As of October 1, 2026, the VAT registration threshold will increase from $200,000 to $350,000 BBD. Certain tourism services, like rental cars with 60% foreign exchange revenue, are subject to a reduced VAT rate of 10%.
*   **Capital Gains Tax:** There is no capital gains tax in Barbados.
*   **National Insurance Contributions:** Employee rates are 11.00% and employer rates are 12.75% up to a maximum insurable earning of BBD 5,360 per month for income year 2026. A Resilience and Regeneration Fund contribution of 0.25% by both employee and employer on total income (less certain allowances) is effective from April 1, 2025.
*   **Double Taxation:** Barbados has 33 double taxation agreements to mitigate being taxed twice on overseas income.
local_tips:
*   **Cost of Living:** Barbados can be more expensive than some other Caribbean islands, especially for imported goods and luxury properties. A single person's estimated monthly costs, excluding rent, can be around $798 USD. A family of four can expect average monthly expenses of around $5,300-$5,500 USD including rent for a comfortable three-bedroom home.
*   **Language:** While English is the official language, the local Bajan dialect (an English-based creole influenced by West African languages) is widely spoken in informal settings. Many Bajans are happy to switch to standard English if visitors struggle to understand the dialect.
*   **Safety:** Barbados is generally considered a safe destination with low crime rates, particularly in tourist areas. However, petty crime like pickpocketing can occur in crowded areas. It's advisable to take normal precautions, secure valuables, and avoid unlit areas at night.
*   **Registration & Visas:** For stays longer than 6 months, options include a Special Entry Permit (SEP) for retirees or property owners, or the Barbados Welcome Stamp (digital nomad visa) for remote workers. The Welcome Stamp allows a 12-month stay, renewable, requiring an annual income of at least $50,000 USD and valid health insurance. Work permits are generally employer-sponsored for local employment.
*   **Healthcare:** Private healthcare is recommended for expats, with plans typically costing between $150-$300 USD per month per person. Comprehensive health insurance that includes medical evacuation is a smart safety net.
*   **Transportation:** Many retirees choose car rental or occasional taxi use, or walking within towns. Public transport is available, with a one-way ticket costing approximately £1 (around $1.25 USD).
*   **Cultural Etiquette:** Politeness, courtesy, and good manners are highly valued. Greeting strangers and saying 'thank you' are customary.
*   **Driving:** The wearing of any form of camouflage is illegal in Barbados.
